node.title: One Function or Many? The Case For and Against Unified AI Integrity Management
node.reading: Two earlier pieces in this series have laid out the conceptual and institutional case. AI Integrity: a Critical Frontier argued that AI integrity is becoming to intelligent systems what cybersecurity became to software. The Case for AI Integrity Management as a Formal Enterprise Function mapped the landscape of existing disciplines — ethics, compliance, cybersecurity, operational reliability — and argued that the structural logic of convergence is real. This third paper asks whether a unified function is desirable in principle and achievable in practice. Would a unified AI Integrity Management function produce genuine operational benefits, or would it mostly be a reorganisation on paper — the same specialists doing the same work under a new letterhead?
node.readingSummary: Two earlier pieces in this series have laid out the conceptual and institutional case.

relations: An integrated mission team and a federated integrity function solve different coordination problems and need not share the same governance structure.
La taxonomía de equipos y la propuesta de función de AI Integrity tienen escalas y responsabilidades diferentes.
An integrity function can coordinate common decision conditions while retaining the distinct authority and expertise of its constituent disciplines.
Propuesta organizativa abierta; no función ya adoptada por todos los clientes ni estándar institucional único.
A mission team and a federated integrity function can share explicit decision interfaces without requiring the same organizational structure.
Los modelos Tiger Team no se ordenan en una jerarquía universal; cada tradición responde a un problema y alcance diferentes.
